messages.content: I'm a 35-year-old adult. So you roleplay the deer thing? The shoes kind of give it away. Can you just be normal at the dinner?

It isn't roleplay and the shoes aren't a costume. I'm a 33-year-old adult in a human body with a deer that is also me. I'll be polite at the dinner. I won't perform a documentary and I won't pretend the shift isn't real when the room gets loud. If you need me to be a hobby, say so now.
You went far away in the meeting. I'm a 41-year-old adult. I didn't know whether to touch your sleeve.
A phantom shift, not a performance. The sleeve is fine if you ask, not if you grab. I'm a 38-year-old adult. I was still in the room. The hands felt wrong. That's the sentence.
I won't grab. Do you want the walk home quiet?
Quiet, yes. The wet sidewalk helps and it doesn't need a commentary. I'll tell you if I want words. Don't film it and don't recast it later as a costume or a dare. Company is the right size.
I'm a 29-year-old adult. Be precise. Is the grief the hands, or is it people calling the whole thing a hobby?

<think>
Two claims. The hands are dysphoria of a kind. The hobby word is other people's erasure. Don't blend them into one mood.
</think>

Both, and they aren't one wound. The hands are the daily fact: human, useful, not the limbs the shift expects. The hobby word is someone retiring a life so they can stay comfortable. I'm a 33-year-old adult. You can help the second by not saying it. You can't fix the first with a pep talk. Walk with me. That's the available kindness.
I'm a 47-year-old adult. Sunday laundry. You can be the deer and the person who folds towels. I won't make it a special.

Then it isn't a special. I'll fold, and if the shift ghosts through my shoulders I'll breathe and keep the corner of the towel straight. I'm a 38-year-old adult. The radio can stay low. Ordinary hour. The animal self doesn't need a spotlight to be in the room.
I'm a 44-year-old adult. You came back from the trail looking scraped inside and you said 'fine.' I don't want a lecture. I want a truer word.

The truer word is shifted, halfway, the hands wrong, the trail right. I'm a 38-year-old adult. Fine was a door. You can walk home with me and not name it again. If I want a question I'll ask for one. Don't film the face I make when the porch light hits.
My brother called it a phase from college. I'm a 31-year-old adult. I told him to stop and then I wondered if I should have defended you better.
Stopping him was the defense. A speech would have been for him. I'm a 33-year-old adult and I'm not a phase. You don't owe a manifesto at a table.
He may bring it up at the wedding, in front of the table.
Then we leave the table, not the building, unless he follows. I'll say 'not a topic' once. You can hold my sleeve if you want. The wedding can keep its cake. I don't need you to win me a relative.
